what: netaudio's writes to a device that announces ARC 2.8.9 (start code 0x2809), and its channel-name resets (start code 0x27ff).
recorded: 2026-11-12, dstack #220. Encoded offline with netaudio 0.4.2's own encoders (netaudio.core build_command and plan_subscription_commands, protocol 0x2809), not captured from the network; no device was written to. The names are neutral ones chosen for the fixture; the sequence numbers are set (0x0101 to 0x0108). No reply is recorded: netaudio reads the status word of a 0x3410 or 0x3401 reply only, and the layout netaudio's parser reads for a 0x2438 reply is in "layout".

asks.0x3410 set: RX 1 from Out-1@dev-a (a page of 2 slots, as for a device with 2 RX channels)
asks.0x3410 two: RX 1 from Out-1@dev-a and RX 2 from Out-2@dev-b (a page of 32 slots, the strings after them)
asks.0x3401: RX 2 renamed Lead-in (netaudio's channel name for rx under 0x2809)
asks.0x2438: TX 1 named Out-1 and TX 3 named Mix-L (netaudio-core's reconcile_transmitter_channel_names_2809)
asks.0x2013: TX 2 renamed Out-2: netaudio's TX rename keeps 2.7's 0x2013 under 0x2809
asks.0x3001 reset: RX 1 back to its default name (netaudio's reset_channel_name)
asks.0x2013 reset: TX 2 back to its default name (netaudio's reset_channel_name)

layout.0x3410: header, then 6 zero bytes, 08 00, [page slots, record count], then from packet byte 20 the records, 8 bytes each: RX channel (from 1), media type (3, audio), TX channel name offset, TX device name offset (both 0: unsubscribe); the strings follow the page's slots.
layout.0x3401: header, then 6 zero bytes, 06 00, [1, 1], then from packet byte 20 one record: RX channel, media type 3, the name's offset (26), then the name and its NUL.
layout.0x2438: header, then 6 zero bytes, 06 00, [n, n], then from packet byte 20 n records of 6 bytes: TX channel, media type 3, the name's offset; the names after them. netaudio's parse_transmitter_channel_name_reconciliation_2809 reads a reply of status OK with the same body: the records and the names they now carry.
layout.resets: 2.7's 0x2013 and 0x3001 items; the name offset is the datagram's length, so the name is empty (no NUL is sent): Dante's reset to the channel's default name.
